comparison.reason: Previous run used macOS arm64 / Apple M1 Pro; this run uses Windows x64 / Ryzen 9 7900X and an expanded suite. No cross-run performance attribution.
comparison.previous_summary_encoding: UTF-8 JSON; ensure_ascii=False; sorted keys; separators=(',', ':'); no trailing newline

limitations: Windows x64 / Ryzen 9 7900X / Release with ThinLTO only.
Complete workloads use reloadable optimized JIT; native free-call optimized JIT is closed-program. Native class modes are separate.
Ratios include language entry, runtime safety, ownership and GC contracts. No timing overhead is subtracted and no samples are discarded.
The C++ reflection reference has fixed receiver and signature contracts without Vela's full GC, reload and dynamic argument behavior.
Direct reflection controls allow inlining and redundant-access elimination; per-operation numbers amortize a 128-operation batch.
CPU frequency scaling and system scheduling may contribute to variation; all measured CVs are retained.

root_cause: The commit lowers public script instance methods through selector-indexed CallVirtual instead of the former direct Call.
JIT direct-call planning and scalar receiver-field inlining handle Call and resolved CallIndirect, while CallVirtual retains the runtime virtual-call helper.
The same commit adds closed instance-call devirtualization in the AOT preparation path; the JIT pipeline does not run that AOT transformation.
The unchanged direct-call benchmark therefore loses JIT method inlining while C++ and AOT keep their small optimized loop.
